Assert that key columns identify each row uniquely

Source: R/ensure_unique.R
ensure_unique.Rd

A checkpoint for keys: every combination of the selected columns must occur at most once. On failure the duplicated rows are reported (see checkpoints) grouped by a dupid column, so each group of copies can be inspected together. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_unique(data, ..., success_msg = NULL, warn_msg = NULL, abort_msg = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

...

Key columns (tidy-select). If omitted, all columns are used, which checks for fully duplicated rows.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when duplicates exist and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description naming the key columns.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

The most valuable place for it is just before a join. A lookup table with a duplicated key makes left_join() silently multiply rows; checking the key first turns that into an explicit message:

codes |>
  ensure_unique(branche, abort_msg = "Codebook has duplicate codes") |>
  left_join(x = df, by = "branche")

It is fast on a population register: the key is grouped without sorting it, and the full rows are only touched when there are duplicates to report.

See also

ensure_balanced() for unit-periods, checkpoints.

Examples

persons <- data.frame(
  cpr  = c("a", "b", "b", "c"),
  year = c(2024, 2024, 2024, 2024)
)

# Success: one row per person
ensure_unique(persons[persons$cpr != "b", ], cpr, year)
#> ✔ Unique on cpr, year

# Warning: b appears twice in 2024
ensure_unique(persons, cpr, year)
#> Warning: Duplicate rows on cpr, year
#> ℹ 2 rows in 1 group:
#>     dupid cpr    year
#>     <int> <chr> <dbl>
#>   1     1 b      2024
#>   2     1 b      2024

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
df |>
  ensure_unique(cvr, year, abort_msg = "Duplicate company-years")
} # }
